gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-blinker: Pixel-bright and a bit cheeky. Early GameBoy has a slight charcoal-stick pressure in its strokes, while Blinker, a plain sans, keeps every line smooth and puts its lowercase to work filling the height.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-carrois-goth: Wide-spaced and cheeky, Early GameBoy has strokes that shift just enough to notice. Carrois Gothic, a plain sans, sets a high x-height and generous c openings, so a long passage would flow without a snag.

Stretched-out tracking is the first thing you notice in Early GameBoy, with its crossbars a touch thinner than the stems. Carrois Gothic SC, a plain sans, is the quiet worker, keeping capitals and lowercase nearly level and every curve ending open.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-chocolate-cl: Chocolate Classical Sans reads big and friendly, its broad-nibbed strokes never curling shut. Early GameBoy brings the thick-thin flicker up top, so the sans below can simply carry the words.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-comme: Early GameBoy stretches its letters wide and keeps sturdy hairlines beside moderate stems, with real swagger for a display face. Comme, a smooth sans-serif, handles the rest.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-cossette-tex: Chunky, wide-set and a little cheeky. Early GameBoy has subtle thick-thin modulation, and Cossette Texte, a plain sans, flattens everything into stencil-like lines with a prominent x-height.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-fresca: Fresca reads smooth and uncalligraphic, with short ascenders over big bowls and counters that stay open to the outside. Early GameBoy contributes the restrained thick-thin play of a worn wooden stamp, and the sans-serif body never mixes bold and light strokes in a word.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-funnel-sans: Early GameBoy spaces its letters wide and gives each word a modest thick and thin rhythm. Funnel Sans answers it with horizontals no thinner than its verticals, a sans that simply stays put.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-gafata: Its strokes sit between monoline and sharply contrasted. Early GameBoy earns its keep big and brief, while Gafata, a sans-serif with a tall letter band and wide-eyed e, handles the rest.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-geist: Playful from the first glyph, Early GameBoy tightens its strokes slightly at curve tops. Geist, a plain sans with hairline-free strokes, would read in solid, quiet blocks over a long passage.
